paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning learns decisions from a fixed dataset. When a policy considers actions unlike those represented in that data, it must estimate outcomes without direct support. These extrapolation errors can compound across a sequence of decisions. The paper starts from the observation that some departures from recorded behavior may matter more to the final outcome than others.

The proposed method places an explicit budget on decisions that differ from the behavior policy. Dynamic programming determines where to spend that budget: which steps warrant trying an unsupported action and which should remain closer to recorded behavior. This makes the tradeoff between potential improvement and extrapolation risk part of the sequential decision problem itself.

The theoretical result establishes constrained optimality of the fixed point of the proposed Q-value updates. That means optimality within the imposed budget, rather than unrestricted optimality. Experiments report better overall performance than state-of-the-art offline reinforcement learning methods on evaluated D4RL tasks, supporting the value of allocating departures selectively.
neurips-2023-budgeting-counterfactual-fo.tldr: The method budgets departures from recorded behavior and uses dynamic programming to decide where those departures are most worthwhile.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to infer which of two variables causes the other. It focuses on location-scale noise models, which describe an effect using its proposed cause and noise whose scale can vary. These models offer expressive relationships alongside identifiability guarantees, making the choice of causal direction a meaningful model-selection problem.

One selection strategy chooses the direction with the highest likelihood. The authors find that this strategy achieves state-of-the-art accuracy when the assumed noise distribution is correct, but its accuracy drops sharply when that distribution is misspecified. Their analysis locates the main failure pattern: the direction opposite to the true causal relationship has smaller conditional variance.

The alternative evaluates whether fitted residuals are independent of the proposed cause. Across the empirical evaluation, this approach is much more robust to incorrect noise assumptions and misleading conditional variance. The contribution therefore concerns how to select between causal models reliably: a strong likelihood result under correct specification does not ensure comparable reliability when the noise model is wrong.
neurips-2023-cause-effect-inference-in-l.tldr: Residual independence testing is empirically more robust than likelihood-based causal direction selection when the assumed noise distribution is wrong.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning must improve a policy without collecting new experience from the environment. This makes actions outside the recorded data distribution difficult to value reliably. Existing approaches restrict actions or deliberately lower estimated values, but these safeguards can be excessively conservative or fail to locate unsupported regions accurately.

CPED addresses this problem by explicitly estimating the density of the behavior policy using a flow-GAN model. This estimate identifies a region supported by the recorded behavior, within which the learned policy can explore alternatives. Here, the safe region refers to support for offline learning decisions; its role is to permit improvement while controlling exposure to unreliable value estimates.

The paper provides theoretical results for the density estimator and a performance guarantee showing that CPED can find the optimal Q-function value. Experiments on standard offline reinforcement learning tasks report higher expected returns than existing alternatives. Together, these results support using an explicit account of behavior density to make policy constraints less conservative.
neurips-2023-constrained-policy-optimiza.tldr: CPED estimates behavior-policy density explicitly to support less conservative offline policy improvement within a data-supported region.

paragraphs: Deep clustering seeks meaningful groups using learned representations. Recent approaches encourage nearby examples to have consistent semantic structure, building on self-supervised methods that distinguish individual instances. However, an immediate neighborhood can contain closely similar examples that offer limited diversity. The paper asks how to obtain more informative supervision from the choice of neighbors.

The proposed Contextually Affinitive Neighborhood uses an efficient online re-ranking procedure inspired by image retrieval. It mines informative neighbors and encourages neighborhood consistency across different views. This changes which relationships guide representation learning, rather than relying exclusively on the closest examples in the current representation.

Neighbors near cluster boundaries can also be misleading. A progressively relaxed boundary filter addresses this noise while the neighborhood-based learning proceeds. The method integrates into general self-supervised frameworks and outperforms state-of-the-art methods on several evaluated benchmarks. Its contribution combines two complementary adjustments: making neighborhoods more informative and reducing the influence of unreliable relationships around group boundaries.
neurips-2023-contextually-affinitive-nei.tldr: The method improves deep clustering by re-ranking informative neighbors and filtering noisy relationships near cluster boundaries.

paragraphs: Remote sensing provides abundant imagery from different sensors but relatively few labels. CROMA learns representations from optical and radar observations aligned in both location and time. Its training combines two tasks: bringing corresponding sensor representations into agreement and reconstructing image patches that have been hidden.

Separate encoders process the partially masked optical and radar inputs for cross-modal contrastive learning. Another encoder combines the sensor information, and a lightweight decoder uses that joint representation to predict missing patches. The authors show that these objectives complement each other for spatially aligned multimodal data, producing representations usable with individual sensors or combined inputs.

CROMA also introduces spatial biases in self-attention and cross-attention through 2D-ALiBi and X-ALiBi. These improve representations and support test images up to 17.6 times larger. Evaluations report improvements over the compared leading multispectral model across classification, probing, clustering, and segmentation. The findings indicate that the learned features support multiple downstream uses, rather than gains being confined to a single evaluation procedure.
neurips-2023-croma-remote-sensing-repres.tldr: CROMA combines radar–optical contrastive learning and masked reconstruction to learn versatile remote-sensing representations.

paragraphs: DataPerf shifts evaluation toward the datasets and data-processing choices that shape machine learning performance. The paper argues that concentrating on model architectures while treating standard datasets as fixed can obscure weaknesses in how well benchmarks represent real problems. It connects this neglect of data to inaccurate, biased, and fragile applications.

The contribution is a community-led benchmark suite and an open online platform for repeated challenges. Participants can improve datasets and data-centric algorithms across successive rounds, with competition, comparable evaluation, and reproducibility supporting that process. This gives dataset development a structured place in research evaluation alongside architecture development.

The first release contains five benchmarks spanning vision, speech, acquisition, debugging, and diffusion prompting. The platform also supports additional community-contributed benchmarks. Its benchmarks, evaluation platform, and baseline implementations are open source, with maintenance assigned to MLCommons. The stated contribution is infrastructure for sustained iteration on data quality and methods, rather than a claim that one particular dataset intervention solves the broader problems identified.
neurips-2023-dataperf-benchmarks-for-dat.tldr: DataPerf provides open benchmarks and recurring challenges for evaluating improvements to datasets and data-centric machine learning methods.

paragraphs: Differentiable Blocks World builds a compact three-dimensional scene description from calibrated images. Its target is a small collection of textured geometric primitives that people can interpret and manipulate. Such a representation also supports physical simulation, giving the reconstruction a practical role beyond reproducing how a scene looks.

The method represents primitives as textured superquadric meshes and optimizes their parameters from scratch. Differentiable rendering connects the current three-dimensional description to rendered images, allowing image mismatch to guide fitting. Each primitive also has transparency, which the authors identify as crucial for optimization and for accommodating varying numbers of primitives.

The reported results show faithful reconstruction of input images and accurate modeling of visible three-dimensional points, alongside completion of unseen object regions. Comparisons use diverse DTU scenes, while additional real captures from BlendedMVS and Nerfstudio demonstrate robustness. Scene editing and physical simulation examples show why a compact primitive decomposition is useful: the recovered scene consists of manipulable components rather than only a visual reconstruction.
neurips-2023-differentiable-blocks-world.tldr: Differentiable Blocks World reconstructs calibrated images as compact collections of textured 3D primitives suitable for editing and simulation.

paragraphs: Control barrier functions describe safety through a nonnegative value that a controller must maintain over time. Neural networks can represent these functions flexibly, but learning a candidate does not itself verify safety. With ReLU networks, a specific obstacle is that the barrier has corners where derivatives are undefined, so verification methods requiring smoothness do not apply.

The paper derives necessary and sufficient safety conditions using a version of Nagumo's theorem that handles sets with nonsmooth boundaries. Its verification algorithm decomposes the neural barrier into linear pieces and solves nonlinear programs to check the pieces and their intersections. Checking intersections is central because they include the places where smooth reasoning breaks down.

To reduce computation, the algorithm concentrates on the safe region's boundary and prunes pieces using interval bound propagation and linear relaxation. Numerical studies compare it with state-of-the-art SMT-based approaches. The main contribution is an exact verification framework tailored to feedforward ReLU barriers, including their nondifferentiable structure.
neurips-2023-exact-verification-of-relu-.tldr: The paper derives exact safety conditions and verification algorithms that account for the corners in ReLU neural control barrier functions.

paragraphs: Conditional stochastic optimization appears in tasks including invariant learning, precision–recall optimization, and meta-learning. When the relevant data are distributed, training must also manage communication among participants. This paper studies the nonconvex version of that optimization problem in federated learning, bringing the conditional sampling structure into the design and analysis of distributed algorithms.

The authors introduce FCSG, which uses a conditional stochastic gradient estimator, and FCSG-M, which adds momentum. They then develop Acc-FCSG-M, an accelerated variant using variance reduction. The sequence of methods addresses both how stochastic updates are estimated and how efficiently those updates support distributed optimization.

The accelerated algorithm is designed to match the single-machine lower bound while achieving the stated best sample and communication complexity. The analysis also explicitly considers task sampling, distinguishing it from the existing federated meta-learning analysis discussed in the paper. Experiments across various tasks validate the algorithms' efficiency, supporting the theoretical emphasis on reducing sampling and communication costs together.
neurips-2023-federated-conditional-stoch.tldr: The paper develops federated algorithms for conditional stochastic optimization, using momentum and variance reduction to improve sampling and communication efficiency.

paragraphs: This paper locates a ground camera by aligning its image with a GPS-tagged satellite image of the same area. The central difficulty is the large viewpoint difference between ground and aerial observations. A differentiable spherical transformation brings the ground image into a matching view and plane, turning localization into an image-alignment problem.

A correlation-aware homography estimator then aligns corresponding parts of the transformed image and satellite image. It is designed to handle occlusion, limited overlap, and seasonal changes. The resulting transformation maps the ground image's center into the satellite image to obtain position, while a point above the central axis provides camera orientation.

The method reports sub-pixel alignment resolution, meter-level GPS accuracy, and operation at 30 frames per second. Mean localization error falls by 21.3% and 32.4% on VIGOR's same-area and cross-area evaluations, respectively, and by 34.4% on KITTI's same-area evaluation against the stated leading techniques. These findings support the effectiveness of combining explicit geometry with robust correspondence estimation.
neurips-2023-fine-grained-cross-view-geo.tldr: The method combines geometric image transformation and robust homography estimation to recover camera position and orientation from satellite imagery.

paragraphs: Researchers often propose brain-learning algorithms inspired by machine learning and describe them as biologically plausible. Such claims frequently depend on whether a synapse could access the information its update rule requires. The paper argues that informal uses of locality in space and time leave those requirements unclear, making biological predictions difficult to assess.

The authors introduce formal, operational definitions covering different classes of locality. Each class specifies which quantities a learning rule cannot use if it is to satisfy a particular biological constraint. This turns a broad plausibility label into explicit restrictions on the information available to the proposed learning mechanism.

The framework is then used to derive testable predictions from classes of synaptic plasticity models. These predictions remain robust to arbitrary choices of neural network architecture, helping separate claims about learning rules from incidental modeling choices. The contribution is a way to sharpen biological hypotheses and identify possible experiments that could falsify a proposed algorithm, rather than evidence that any one algorithm is implemented by the brain.
neurips-2023-formalizing-locality-for-no.tldr: The paper formalizes locality constraints on synaptic learning rules so biological plausibility claims yield testable predictions.

paragraphs: This paper analyzes how neural network size and initialization affect information leakage during randomized training. It measures privacy through a bound on KL divergence between model distributions produced from worst-case neighboring datasets. The focus is fully connected networks and the roles of width, depth, and the initial distribution of parameter values.

The analysis identifies the expected squared norm of parameter gradients during training as a major determinant of the privacy bound. In the special case of a linearized network, this quantity is directly tied to each layer's initialization variance. Initialization therefore changes how network depth affects the bound, even within the same broad model family.

Under the analyzed settings, increasing depth improves the privacy bound for LeCun and Xavier initialization but worsens it for He and NTK initialization. The authors also bound excess empirical risk under a fixed KL privacy budget and find a similarly initialization-dependent relationship with depth. The results concern these analytical bounds and show why depth alone is insufficient to characterize the privacy–utility tradeoff.
neurips-2023-initialization-matters-priv.tldr: The analysis shows that initialization can reverse how increasing network depth affects privacy bounds and the privacy–utility tradeoff.

paragraphs: Ensemble reinforcement learning combines multiple models to improve decision making and value estimation. Yet having several sub-policies does not necessarily produce sufficiently varied experience. The paper analyzes existing ensemble methods and finds that limited diversity among their sub-policies may restrict sample efficiency, reducing the benefit obtained from each interaction with the environment.

The proposed algorithm, TEEN, pursues high expected return while encouraging diverse trajectories. A trajectory is the sequence of experience generated as decisions unfold, so the diversity objective concerns how policies move through the task over time. This connects exploration to the variety of complete experiences produced by the ensemble.

Experiments show that TEEN increases the ensemble policy's sample diversity compared with using sub-policies alone and improves performance over the evaluated ensemble algorithms. The reported average performance gain is 41% across the tested representative environments. These results support the paper's diagnosis that trajectory diversity is a useful design target, with the numerical improvement applying to its evaluated settings.
neurips-2023-keep-various-trajectories-p.tldr: TEEN promotes diverse trajectories alongside reward maximization, improving exploration and average performance in the tested ensemble reinforcement learning environments.

paragraphs: Vision–language models can classify images using category descriptions without labeled examples for those categories. However, this zero-shot ability still falls short of dedicated classifiers trained with supervised fine-tuning. LaFTer investigates how much of that gap can be reduced using an unlabeled image collection and language describing the categories of interest.

The method uses a large language model to generate category descriptions that effectively substitute for labeled visual instances during adaptation. It requires neither image labels nor paired vision–language data for this tuning. The categories still guide the generated text, providing semantic information that can be combined with the unlabeled image collection.

Across the evaluated datasets, the approach reports absolute improvements of up to 11.7%, averaging 3.8%, over the compared zero-shot performance and contemporary methods. It also reports an average 1.3% gain over leading prompting baselines using five-shot supervision. These findings show that language-generated category information can provide useful adaptation signals even when labeled images are unavailable.
neurips-2023-lafter-label-free-tuning-of.tldr: LaFTer improves zero-shot image classification using unlabeled images and language-model-generated category descriptions without paired image–text training data.

paragraphs: The paper examines creative problem solving through the ability to find connections among words. It draws on cognitive research in which misleading associations can cause people to fixate on an unhelpful solution. The authors argue that this aspect of human-like behavior has received little attention in language-model evaluation.

They introduce the Only Connect Wall dataset from a quiz format containing deliberately misleading clues. Models must group clue words using varied kinds of connections and identify the correct connection within each group. This setting makes an attractive but incorrect association part of the problem, providing a proxy for studying fixation and the Einstellung effect in language models.

The study evaluates selected pretrained language models and LLMs, including GPT models, and creates OCW-Randomized and OCW-WordNet as additional synthetic datasets to investigate its red-herring hypothesis. The title frames the work around model fixation, while the abstract describes the evaluation without numerical outcomes. Its concrete contribution is a dataset and experimental setup for examining how misleading associations interact with connection-based problem solving.
neurips-2023-large-language-models-are-f.tldr: The paper introduces word-connection datasets to investigate creative problem solving and fixation on misleading associations in language models.

paragraphs: Different tasks in the same environment often share safety requirements. A kitchen robot, for example, should avoid breaking plates regardless of its immediate assignment. The paper studies how to learn such shared constraints from demonstrations of successful, safe behavior, reducing reliance on manually written rules that can be laborious and error-prone.

The approach extends inverse reinforcement learning to infer constraints. Its guiding idea is that an expert's refusal to take a highly rewarding action may reveal that the action is forbidden. However, interpreting omissions is ambiguous: many constraints could explain the same demonstration, including overly restrictive rules that prohibit every behavior the expert did not show.

The authors address this ambiguity through diverse demonstrations from multiple tasks. Different tasks expose a broader range of acceptable behavior, helping the method learn a tighter set of constraints without rejecting so much unobserved behavior. Simulation experiments on high-dimensional continuous-control tasks validate the approach. The central insight is that task diversity supplies information about shared safety boundaries.
neurips-2023-learning-shared-safety-cons.tldr: The method uses demonstrations across multiple tasks to infer shared safety constraints while reducing overly conservative restrictions.

paragraphs: M3Exam evaluates language models using real official examination questions. The authors argue that human exams bring together language comprehension, subject knowledge, and problem solving, making them useful for assessing a broader range of abilities. The benchmark adds variation across languages, visual content, and educational stages rather than concentrating on one evaluation setting.

The collection contains 12,317 questions in nine languages across three educational levels. About 23% require image processing to solve successfully. Questions from different countries also draw on cultural knowledge, so multilingual evaluation involves more than recognizing the wording of a translated question.

Evaluations find that the tested leading models, including GPT-4, struggle with multilingual text, particularly low-resource languages and languages using non-Latin scripts. The tested multimodal models also perform poorly on complex questions combining modalities. These findings identify gaps in the models evaluated by the study and motivate using the benchmark to track progress across several abilities together. Data and evaluation code are released to support that use.
neurips-2023-m3exam-a-multilingual-multi.tldr: M3Exam uses official exams across nine languages and three educational levels to reveal multilingual and multimodal weaknesses in the evaluated LLMs.

paragraphs: Survival regression models the timing of events using observed characteristics. Neural versions can capture nonlinear relationships, but their flexibility may still be constrained by a proportional-hazard assumption. The Neural Frailty Machine introduces multiplicative frailty as a principled way to extend that assumption while retaining the approximation capabilities of neural networks.

The framework produces two concrete models, extending neural proportional-hazard models and nonparametric hazard regression models. Both can be trained efficiently by maximizing likelihood. This combines a classical survival-analysis modeling idea with neural components, giving the framework ways to represent relationships beyond those covered by its starting models.

For both models, the authors establish convergence-rate guarantees for neural approximation of the nonparametric components. Synthetic experiments support the theoretical statements, and evaluations on six benchmark datasets of different sizes assess prediction quality. Performance is comparable to, and sometimes better than, state-of-the-art survival models. The findings support additional modeling flexibility without claiming that the proposed models outperform every alternative on every dataset.
neurips-2023-neural-frailty-machine-beyo.tldr: Neural Frailty Machine uses multiplicative frailty to extend neural survival models beyond proportional hazards, with theoretical guarantees and competitive benchmark performance.

paragraphs: Non-autoregressive translation accelerates inference, but conventional models assume that target tokens are conditionally independent. That assumption limits how they represent relationships among the words in a translation and contributes to a quality gap relative to autoregressive models. The paper targets this loss of expressive power in the output model.

PCFG-NAT introduces a specially designed probabilistic context-free grammar to represent more complex dependencies among output tokens. The grammar supplies a structured account of how sentence components relate, allowing the translation model to capture connections that independent token predictions struggle to express. The approach therefore addresses the dependency assumption at the center of the stated problem.

Experiments on major translation benchmarks show that PCFG-NAT further narrows the quality gap between non-autoregressive and autoregressive systems. The authors also describe the grammatical structure as helping explain generated sentences, addressing interpretability alongside translation quality. The reported conclusion is an improvement in that tradeoff, rather than a claim that the remaining quality gap has disappeared.
neurips-2023-non-autoregressive-machine-.tldr: PCFG-NAT adds probabilistic grammar structure to non-autoregressive translation to capture token dependencies and narrow the translation-quality gap.

paragraphs: Some learning objectives combine functions inside other functions and sum many such coupled terms. Existing work on finite-sum coupled compositional optimization assumes smooth inner and outer functions. This paper broadens the setting to nonsmooth, weakly convex functions, allowing a class of objectives excluded by those smoothness requirements.

The analyzed setting requires a weakly convex, non-decreasing outer function and a weakly convex inner function. The authors study a single-loop algorithm and bound the work needed to find an approximately stationary point of the objective's Moreau envelope, a smoothed representation used in the analysis. This is a stationarity guarantee, rather than a guarantee of finding a global optimum.

The algorithm is also extended to a three-level composition, where three functions are nested. Applications include deep-learning objectives for two-way partial AUC maximization and its multi-instance version. Empirical studies demonstrate effectiveness on these applications, linking the broader optimization theory to concrete learning objectives while retaining explicit structural assumptions on the functions.
neurips-2023-non-smooth-weakly-convex-fi.tldr: The paper extends coupled compositional optimization to nonsmooth weakly convex objectives and analyzes algorithms for two-level and three-level compositions.

paragraphs: Normalization equivariance means that shifting or scaling an input produces a corresponding change in the output. Standard neural networks do not guarantee this behavior, even when it is desirable for a processing task. This paper develops architectural changes that make the property hold by construction rather than depend on what training happens to learn.

The proposed design replaces ordinary convolutions with affine-constrained convolutions and replaces element-wise activation functions, including ReLU, with channel-wise sort pooling. The authors argue that both kinds of replacement are needed in their methodology. Together, these operations preserve the desired response to shifts and scaling while providing better-conditioned alternatives.

Image-denoising experiments show that the modified networks retain performance and generalize much better across noise levels. This matters because the architectural property governs how the network responds when input normalization changes, while the experiments test a practical benefit in denoising. The evidence supports the proposed design for that application without requiring the property to emerge indirectly from training examples.
neurips-2023-normalization-equivariant-n.tldr: The paper redesigns convolutions and activations to guarantee shift-and-scale equivariance and improve denoising generalization across noise levels.

paragraphs: A two-sample test asks whether two collections of observations come from different distributions. This paper also asks where statistically significant differences occur. Locating those differences provides a more detailed result than a single overall decision, but examining multiple regions requires care to avoid accumulating false discoveries.

The proposed ME_MaBiD test combines multiple Mahalanobis kernels with a bidirectional testing hypothesis to use local information. For regional analysis, the method divides the embedding space into rectangular regions using a splitting criterion tied to test power and data correlation. It then combines the test with a bidirectional masked p-value to investigate local differences.

The theoretical analysis supplies an asymptotic distribution and lower bounds on test power for ME_MaBiD. It also controls the familywise error rate in the local search, addressing the risk of making at least one false rejection across the explored regions. Extensive experiments validate both overall two-sample testing and the identification of local significant differences, connecting detection with more informative localization.
neurips-2023-on-the-exploration-of-local.tldr: ME_MaBiD combines a two-sample test with regional analysis to locate significant distribution differences while controlling familywise error.

paragraphs: OpenAGI is an open-source platform for studying how language models can combine specialized capabilities to solve multi-step tasks. A task arrives as a natural-language request, and the language model selects and executes appropriate expert models. The motivation is that coordinating available skills is itself an important component of solving complex problems.

The platform supports two complementary kinds of work. Standard benchmark tasks enable evaluation and comparison, while open-ended tasks allow expansion through additional models, tools, plugins, and APIs. This gives researchers a common setting for assessing established tasks while exploring new combinations of capabilities.

The paper also proposes Reinforcement Learning from Task Feedback, which uses task outcomes to improve the language model's problem-solving ability. The intended feedback loop links execution results to future task handling. Code, data, benchmarks, evaluation methods, and a demonstration interface are released. The authors present integration of general language-model abilities with specialized expertise as a promising research direction toward AGI, while explicitly recognizing that AGI has no single defined solution path.
neurips-2023-openagi-when-llm-meets-doma.tldr: OpenAGI provides a platform where LLMs coordinate expert models and use task feedback to improve multi-step problem solving.

paragraphs: Estimating individual treatment effects from observational data is difficult because treatment groups differ through selection bias. Many methods align their learned representations by measuring distribution discrepancy. This paper identifies two ways that measurement can become misleading: poorly balanced mini-batches containing outliers, and calculations that omit the effects of unobserved confounders.

The proposed Entire Space CounterFactual Regression method, ESCFR, modifies an optimal-transport framework to address these issues. A relaxed mass-preserving regularizer targets mini-batch sampling effects. A proximal factual outcome regularizer targets unobserved-confounder effects. Both changes focus on improving the discrepancy signal that guides alignment and estimator training.

Experiments report more accurate discrepancy estimates, more effective handling of treatment selection bias, and significantly better performance than prevalent competitors. These findings support the proposed regularizers in the evaluated settings. The contribution centers on making distribution alignment more reliable when its inputs are distorted by sampling and confounding effects; the reported empirical results do not establish universal recovery of causal effects under arbitrary hidden confounding.
neurips-2023-optimal-transport-for-treat.tldr: ESCFR modifies optimal-transport alignment to address mini-batch distortions and unobserved-confounder effects in treatment-effect estimation.

paragraphs: Rotation synchronization seeks to recover underlying rotations from information that may be corrupted. ReSync tackles a robust formulation directly on the rotation group, keeping the optimization within the space of valid rotations. Its least-unsquared objective is both nonsmooth and nonconvex, so the analysis must handle more than ordinary smooth minimization.

The algorithm uses Riemannian subgradients, and its theoretical justification proceeds in stages under a random corruption setting. First, the initialization is shown to land in a suitable neighborhood of the true rotations. Next, the authors establish weak sharpness, a property of the objective that supports a local convergence argument.

Combining these results yields linear convergence to the true rotations under appropriate conditions. Linear convergence describes a geometric reduction in error as iterations proceed, making the guarantee stronger than simply approaching a stationary point. The initialization result matters because it places the method where the local guarantee applies. Experiments demonstrate effectiveness, complementing the conditional theory with numerical evidence.
neurips-2023-resync-riemannian-subgradie.tldr: ReSync directly optimizes rotations and achieves linear convergence to the true solution under appropriate random-corruption conditions.
